Quick update from infra/proxy side after reviewing the redirect_trace.txt: we see a repeated POST -> 302 -> 302 -> GET pattern where the second 302 resolves to our coupa-redirect endpoint but with an Authorization header stripped by an intermediate proxy (idp.specterco.com) on the third hop. When Authorization gets dropped, the coupa-redirect responds with a 502 from the backend (it expects the signed token).

Hypothesis: the intermediate proxy rewrites headers for long redirect sequences and strips hop-specific auth on redirects over 2 hops. This appears to be a difference in behavior between the customer's proxy chain and the typical single-idp flow we test.

Immediate asks:
- Can we generate a one-time pre-signed acceptance URL that embeds the minimal token so the flow finishes in a single redirect? If engineering can't produce a new URL type quickly, can we generate a short-lived token (30 minutes) and a direct activation endpoint that accepts it?
- Jonas, please confirm whether any WAF rules touched coupa-redirect in the last 24 hours. If not, we can rule out our own configuration change.

I'll keep digging on header logs. Attaching the error snippet from the coupa-redirect logs.

—Ben
Sr. Ops Engineer
Redwood Inference
